question: What happened to TikTok's ownership and US operations in 2025?
text:
TikTok briefly went dark in the U.S. in January 2025, then resumed service and stayed online while the Trump administration delayed enforcement of a federal divest-or-ban law. ByteDance signed a deal in December to give up majority control of key U.S. operations, but **the deal didn’t close until January 22, 2026**. ([everycrsreport.com](https://www.everycrsreport.com/reports/R48023.html?utm_source=openai))

- **January–February:** The Supreme Court upheld the law on January 17. TikTok went offline late January 18 as the law was about to take effect, then restored service on January 19 after President-elect Trump promised to delay enforcement. Apple and Google didn’t restore it to their U.S. app stores until February 13. ([supremecourt.gov](https://www.supremecourt.gov/opinions/24pdf/24-656_new_3dq3.pdf?utm_source=openai))
- **September–December:** After several enforcement delays, Trump approved a framework on September 25 for a majority-American-owned joint venture. On December 18, TikTok and ByteDance signed binding agreements with Oracle, Silver Lake, and Abu Dhabi-based MGX. ([govinfo.gov](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/DCPD-202500957/html/DCPD-202500957.htm))
- **What changed at closing:** Oracle, Silver Lake, and MGX each took **15%** of the new U.S. joint venture, and ByteDance kept **19.9%**. The venture took responsibility for U.S. user data, recommendation-algorithm security, and content moderation. It wasn’t a sale of TikTok globally: U.S. users remained connected to the global platform, and TikTok’s global business retained certain commercial functions, including advertising and e-commerce. ([axios.com](https://www.axios.com/2026/01/23/tiktok-deal-trump-app-ban?utm_source=openai))
